correctness.rationale: For k<n/2 two span-k chords have strict interior crossing iff the relative start offset belongs to 1..k-1 or n-k+1..n-1, yielding 2(k−1)/n and L uniform. Their supporting lines have common normal distance cos(πk/n) and angular displacement 2πJ/n; solving gives R=sin(πδ/n)/sin(π(δ+L)/n), δ=n/2-k. Weak convergence of (δ+L)/n to Uniform(0,1/2) yields nR Pareto-type limit. Improper Riemann sum for 0<q<1, harmonic estimate at q=1, dominated fixed-index series for q>1, and uniform q=1+λ/log n expansion give the exact constants and critical window. The rare-event staircase includes equality because sin(x)/x strictly decreases. Fresh Cartesian line-intersection solution matched each atom across 930 admissible (n,k) cases for n=5..64.
residual_risks: The asymptotics hold for fixed integer or half-integer δ with its mandated n parity; a finite exact law and finite numerical cases alone would not establish all-n limits.

evidence: Full published interior-pair theorem computes 2-term area-uniform point-distance extreme tail; it does not sample diagonal segments or their intersection. A generic line-intersection identity yields local geometry but not discrete conditional near-diameter statistics.
